key_insight: Hidden-parameter coverage and separation govern the approximation accuracy, conditioning, and recovery stability of shallow ReLU^k networks on bounded domains.
engineering_relevance: The results provide theoretical guidance for choosing hidden parameters and assessing coefficient stability in least-squares network fitting.
method: Measure parameter geometry using fill distance h and antipodal separation distance h̲.
Use smooth localization and dyadic Fourier estimates to derive approximation bounds and spectral estimates.
Establish norm discretization, regularized recovery, and inverse approximation results.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds rather than empirical benchmarks, with approximation gains up to regularity (d+2k+1)/2 and saturation-type lower bounds for fixed smoother targets.
watch_item: The upper approximation bound holds on an interior subdomain, while the lower bound concerns the larger domain; they are not directly matching error estimates.
paper_title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation and Stability Properties of Shallow ReLU$^k$ Networks on Bounded Euclidean Domains
